issues.title: Replace advisory allow/deny booleans with a sealed execution capability
issues.finding: Execution authorization is represented as serializable booleans and a conventional `if` branch rather than a required capability. `EffectPreflightReportV1` exposes `blocked/advisory_only/commit_eligible`, `EffectCommitDecisionV1` exposes `commit_authorized`, `verification-policy` exposes `PolicyDecision::allows_execution() -> bool`, and `forge-pilot` branches on that boolean before calling execution.
issues.why_it_matters: This is policy by convention. A downstream caller can bypass the branch and still reach effectful code. The spec requires hard gates, not strongly-worded JSON.
issues.evidence: effect-runtime/src/effect.rs; verification-policy/src/lib.rs:272; forge-pilot/src/loop_runner.rs:440,540,705; llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs
issues.required_changes: Introduce a sealed runtime-only `CommitToken` / `ExecutionPermit` minted only after policy + approval + verification-plan checks. All effectful execution APIs must require that token. Artifacts remain serializable receipts; the token is the runtime enforcement object.
issues.acceptance: No effectful path can be invoked with only booleans or raw strings. `rg -n "CommitToken|ExecutionPermit|ApprovalGrant" verification-policy llm-tool-runtime forge-pilot effect-runtime` returns owned types and use-sites; direct execute signatures without a permit are gone.
issues.proof: rg -n "allows_execution\(|commit_authorized|approval_token" effect-runtime verification-policy llm-tool-runtime forge-pilot && cargo test -p llm-tool-runtime -p forge-pilot
issues.touches: verification-policy/src/lib.rs; verification-policy/src/permit.rs (new); llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs; llm-tool-runtime/src/runtime.rs; forge-pilot/src/loop_runner.rs; forge-pilot/src/act.rs; effect-runtime/src/effect.rs; stack-ids/src/ids.rs

issues.title: Replace `ToolCtx.approval_token: Option<String>` with a typed constitutional grant
issues.finding: `llm-tool-runtime` already has decent enum discipline, but the actual approval carrier is still `Option<String>`. That means the critical approval path is stringly and forgeable by construction.
issues.why_it_matters: A free-form approval token undercuts the very enforcement point that should be strongest. It must be tied to scope, effect class, constitution citation, expiry, and decision lineage.
issues.evidence: llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs:262-291; llm-tool-runtime/src/runtime.rs:33-45; llm-tool-runtime/src/starter_tools.rs:401,493-514
issues.spec_anchors: V9 §5 execution evidence; V11 §8 proof-governed promotion; V16 §8 budget/disclosure/suspension; ENDSTATE §8 and §10
issues.required_changes: Define a typed `ApprovalGrant` or reuse the `CommitToken` family. Carry scope, effect/action class, approver lineage, expiry, decision id, and constitution citation. Read-only fast paths may remain tokenless only if the tool descriptor is provably read-only and non-promoting.
issues.acceptance: `ToolCtx` no longer contains `approval_token: Option<String>`. Approval evaluation accepts a typed grant. Destructive tools cannot be invoked with raw strings.
issues.proof: rg -n "approval_token: Option<String>" llm-tool-runtime/src && cargo test -p llm-tool-runtime
issues.touches: llm-tool-runtime/src/contracts.rs; llm-tool-runtime/src/runtime.rs; llm-tool-runtime/src/starter_tools.rs; forge-pilot/src/act.rs; verification-policy/src/lib.rs

issues.title: Eliminate stringly typed controlled vocabularies from governance and control surfaces
issues.finding: First-wave controlled vocabulary is now enum-backed across the execution, policy, attestation, review-control, delegation, continuity, adjudication, and remote-admission lanes: `effect-runtime` owns the execution vocab (`effect_class`, `blast_radius_ceiling`, `reversibility_class`, `run_mode`, `publication_status`, window/receipt/observation/result vocab), `verification-policy` now types the top-level policy profile vocab (`allowed_run_modes`/`required_preflight_checks`/`required_observation_classes`/`requires_compensation_plan_for`, `forbidden_role_combinations`, `required_assurance_sections`/`required_monitor_classes`, `required_forensic_freeze_surfaces`/`requires_postmortem_for_severity`), its `v14` budget/admission/disclosure vocab (`budget_class`/`max_exactness`/`refuter_allowance`/`oracle_allowance`/`replay_allowance`/`human_review_allowance`/`exhaustion_behavior`, `required_replayability_class`/`downgrade_behavior`, `replay_visibility`, `allowed_reveal_class`), plus the remaining privacy/locality policy lane (`default_retention_class`/`archive_restore_expectation`/`cross_border_transfer_default`, `approval_requirement`/`default_disclosure_budget_class`, `default_decision`, `disclosure_budget_class`/`export_package_format`, `tenant_key_kind`/`isolation_class`/`cross_tenant_query_default`, `required_attestation`/`required_disclosure_policy_class`); `assurance-runtime` now types `publication_status` plus `coverage_state`/`decision_state`/`status`/`trigger_kind`, `attestation-exchange` now types `replayability_class`/`expiration_policy`/`rotation_policy`/`admissibility_judgment` plus the vendor `translation_mode`/`rotation_channel`/`revocation_channel`/`replay_impact`/`admission_impact` lane, `authority-delegation` now types `blast_radius_ceiling`, `current_validity_state`, and `disclosure_ceiling`, `verification-control` now types review-case `final_state`/`block_reason`/`decision_state`, receipt `retry_owner`, and the v14 experiment/refuter/dispute lane (`risk_class`/`lifecycle_state`/`final_disposition`, `refuter_kind`/`state`/`promotion_impact`, `exactness_spend`/`selected_decision`, `current_disposition`, plus `admissibility_judgment`), `verification-adjudication` now types `rollback_scope`/`refutation_class`/`invalidation_radius` plus the v14 `decision_class`/`rollback_class` lane, `continuity-runtime` now types `severity`/`default_severity`/`status`/`replay_state`/`exercise_kind`, and `remote-oracle-admission` now types `exactness_class_ceiling`/`exactness_target`/`exactness_class` plus `disclosure_ceiling`/`allowed_disclosure`/`replay_obligation`/`local_admission_recommendation`/`failure_behavior`. The wider governance/policy/control crates still carry raw controlled vocabulary fields, so this row remains open.
issues.why_it_matters: Schemas will accept nonsense, exhaustive matching is impossible, and semantic drift becomes invisible at compile time. This is the opposite of constitutional enforcement.
issues.evidence: `python3 scripts/check_constitutional_vocab.py` now passes and rejects raw `String`/`Vec<String>` declarations for the effect/policy/assurance/attestation/authority/review-control/adjudication/continuity/remote controlled-vocab lane. `effect-runtime/src/{effect,observation,compensation,vocab}.rs`, `verification-policy/src/{lib,v14,profile_p1_privacy,profile_p2_locality}.rs`, `assurance-runtime/src/{profile,assurance,certification}.rs`, `attestation-exchange/src/{lib,profile_p6_vendor}.rs`, `authority-delegation/src/capability.rs`, `verification-control/src/{lib,v14}.rs`, `verification-adjudication/src/{lib,v14}.rs`, `continuity-runtime/src/{incident,recovery,profile_p7_incident_routing,vocab}.rs`, and `remote-oracle-admission/src/lib.rs` now serialize controlled vocab with stable wire values; `profile-runtime/src/adapters.rs` explicitly bridges the typed policy vocab back to runtime-view strings; the stale `v14` examples in `examples/ExperimentCaseV1.example.json` and `examples/ComparabilityMatrixV1.example.json`, the top-level policy profile examples, and the privacy/locality policy examples now round-trip with those typed wire values; and the checked schemas/examples/fixtures remain compatible after regeneration.
issues.spec_anchors: V6 §2.8 and matrix law; V11 §3, §4, §6, §8; ENDSTATE §5, §7, §17
issues.required_changes: Replace controlled vocabulary strings with enums in owner crates. Add serde-stable `snake_case` wire names. Introduce a repo lint that forbids new `String`-typed controlled vocab fields without an explicit allowlist annotation or script allowlist.
issues.acceptance: All controlled vocab fields are enum-backed or explicitly allowlisted as free text. `scripts/check_constitutional_vocab.py` passes and CI runs it.
issues.proof: rg -n "pub .*: (String|Option<String>|Vec<String>)," effect-runtime assurance-runtime attestation-exchange authority-delegation verification-control verification-adjudication continuity-runtime remote-oracle-admission verification-policy && python3 scripts/check_constitutional_vocab.py
issues.touches: effect-runtime/src/*.rs; verification-policy/src/*.rs; profile-runtime/src/adapters.rs; assurance-runtime/src/*.rs; attestation-exchange/src/*.rs; authority-delegation/src/*.rs; verification-control/src/*.rs; verification-adjudication/src/*.rs; continuity-runtime/src/*.rs; remote-oracle-admission/src/*.rs; contract-schema-gen/src/lib.rs; scripts/check_constitutional_vocab.py

issues.title: Implement reference interpreters for hard semantic seams and wire differential conformance
issues.finding: The repo has real artifact families and some strong bridge tests, but the hard seams are still not formally owned as reference interpreters: execution admissibility, widening/degradation semantics, minimal-change repair, and effect decision chain validity.
issues.why_it_matters: Without reference interpreters, semantics can drift while schemas stay green. Bridge atomicity is partly enforced already; the rest of the hard seams need the same treatment.
issues.evidence: Bridge tests already reject missing `episode_id` for canonical bundle-bearing exports (`forge-memory-bridge/src/transform.rs` and tests). Comparable reference modules are missing for execution admissibility, widening, and repair. The current `conformance/` tree holds manifests/README surfaces but not a unified hard-seam refint harness.
issues.required_changes: Add explicit reference-interpreter modules for: (a) preflight→commit→execution admissibility, (b) widening/degradation outcome classification, (c) minimal-change repair selection, (d) import atomicity / episode bundle requirements. Wire them into `kernel-conformance` and `conformance/*` differential tests.
issues.acceptance: Every hard seam has a reference implementation, golden fixtures, and production-vs-refint differential tests. Semantic drift budget is explicit and gated.
issues.proof: rg -n "refint|reference interpreter|differential" kernel-conformance conformance verification-policy verification-adjudication knowledge-runtime forge-memory-bridge && cargo test -p kernel-conformance -p verification-policy -p forge-memory-bridge

The mandatory-ref gate locks in non-optional `PolicyDecision.plan_id`, permit minting rejection for advisory-only or non-promotable plans, `forge-pilot` verification-plan artifact emission, `remote-oracle-admission` required/returned artifact refs, `effect-runtime` initiating/execution lineage refs, and `forge-memory-bridge` rejection of canonical bundle exports missing `episode_id`; the vocab lint still covers the additional `verification-policy` privacy/locality controlled fields; the docs gate reports `verification-policy` at 49/49 documented public functions; and the gate is green after rerunning the full release-lane test sweep.
